title: Prioritize declared passes within slicer list readiness groups
lead: Make the default list reflect release priority within each existing status/readiness group: earlier declared passes before subsequent passes, then effective score and stored queue order.
findings_note: owner request 2026-10-05: list should prioritize v1.3 over v1.4 and later below defined release passes; preserve status/readiness groups

sections.heading: Why
sections.body: The current list places s208 (v1.4, score 33) ahead of s220 (v1.3, score 32), and s213 (later, score 22) ahead of lower-scoring v1.3 work. Release membership should affect default list priority without displacing the existing status/readiness groups. The owner explicitly chose to preserve those groups and order by pass within each group.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body: src/slicer/cli.py (_list_in_next_order and cmd_list); src/slicer/graph.py (ranked_order, if needed); src/slicer/model.py (Index.passes and pass_keys); tests/test_cli.py (ListNextOrderTests); tests/test_scoring.py; docs/commands.md; README.md.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
1. Within the same status/readiness group, a v1.3 item precedes a v1.4 item even when the v1.4 item's effective score is higher or it occurs earlier in the stored queue.
2. Within that group, items in declared release passes precede later items even when later has a higher effective score.
3. Across different status/readiness groups, the existing group order takes precedence over pass order, including in-work, eligible open, remaining visible, and parked groups.
4. Within a pass and group, descending effective score and stable stored-queue ties remain unchanged, including inherited dependency scores.
5. Custom non-version pass names follow declaration order. Undeclared and empty pass keys remain visible in the fallback group after declared passes. A roadmap without declared passes retains its current ordering.
6. Text, ordinary JSON, and lean JSON return the same item order. Filters keep their existing membership semantics, and a filtered list applies the same ranking to the remaining rows.
7. Explicit --sort score and --sort effort retain their existing flat sort rules; listing does not mutate the stored queue. Existing next, sort, TUI, and generated-render ordering tests continue to pass.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
Preserve default list's existing status/readiness groups as the primary sort key. Within each group, rank items by the roadmap's declared pass order, then descending effective score, then stored queue position. Use the existing ordered pass declarations as the source of priority: this project's sequence has v1.3 before v1.4 and later after the release passes. Keep later last in this project's declared sequence; do not hardcode project-specific pass names or parse pass labels as semantic versions.

Treat items with empty or undeclared pass keys as one fallback rank after all declared passes, preserving effective-score and queue tie rules within that rank. With no declared passes, all items share the fallback rank and existing ordering is preserved.

Apply this to default slicer list output in text and both JSON profiles, including filtered views and --all. Preserve explicit score/effort sorts. Keep this slice limited to list ranking: next selection, persisted sort/move operations, TUI order, and generated roadmap order retain their existing behavior. Avoid changing shared ranked_order behavior for other callers unintentionally.

Update the command reference and README descriptions that currently describe list as next's order. Document pass declaration order, fallback behavior, group precedence, and explicit sort overrides.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body: All seven cases above pass. A fixture with declared passes v1.3, v1.4, later demonstrates release priority despite opposing scores, while a fixture with opposing readiness groups demonstrates that group precedence is preserved. Run focused list/scoring tests, the full unittest suite, slicer check, and git diff --check. Verify that repeated list reads leave tracking state and generated output unchanged.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: One implementation slice in its own worktree. Commit or merge only when the owner requests it.
